title: Product Catalog High-Traffic ISR Cache Stampede / Dog-Piling
businessContext: A leading apparel retailer uses Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) with `revalidate: 60`. During a product drop with 200,000 visitors per minute, when the 60-second cache window expires, thousands of concurrent requests miss cache simultaneously and hit the PostgreSQL database, exhausting connection pools and causing a site-wide 504 Gateway Timeout.
problemStatement: Under high concurrency, when a static page becomes stale, multiple incoming requests trigger parallel background revalidations because there is no single-flight deduplication / distributed lock. Diagnose the cache stampede (dog-piling) and implement a distributed stale-while-revalidate lock / mutex pattern.
constraints: Must maintain high-throughput static caching (sub-20ms P99 for cached reads).
At most 1 revalidation query should hit the database per cache expiry cycle.
Stale content must be served to subsequent shoppers while revalidation is in flight.
candidateTasks: Explain the Cache Stampede (Dog-Piling / Thundering Herd) problem in Next.js ISR.
Implement single-flight promise memoization or Redis distributed lock with `SET NX PX`.
Explain the role of Next.js 15 `unstable_cache` / Cache Handler in multi-instance cluster deployments.
hints: In a single process, a Map of in-flight promises can deduplicate parallel requests.
In a multi-pod Kubernetes cluster, use a distributed cache lock in Redis so only one pod regenerates the cache while others serve stale.

testCases.name: Deduplicates concurrent revalidation calls into single flight
testCases.explanation: Ensures only 1 database query executes during concurrent cache miss.

alternativeApproaches: Probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm) to revalidate before the cache hard-expires.
Active cron-based cache warmers instead of passive on-demand revalidation.
commonMistakes: Simply increasing the cache TTL: that only delays the stampede when it finally expires.
Allowing multiple pods to run revalidation in parallel, wiping out the database connection pool.
